text: Walk me through your background and what brought you here today.
coach: They want a concise narrative arc connecting your past experience to this specific role.

text: Give me your 60-second elevator pitch.
coach: They're testing whether you can distill your value proposition under pressure.

text: How would your current manager describe you in three words?
coach: They want self-awareness and evidence that you understand how others perceive you.

text: What's the common thread across the roles you've held so far?
coach: They're looking for intentionality in your career rather than random job-hopping.

text: Tell me something about yourself that isn't on your resume.
coach: They want to see personality, authenticity, and whether you're a culture add.

text: If you had to summarize your career in a single headline, what would it be?
coach: They're assessing your ability to communicate with clarity and creativity.

text: What are you most proud of professionally, and why?
coach: They want to understand what you value and how you measure personal success.

text: Why are you looking for a change right now?
coach: They're probing for red flags like running away versus running toward something.

text: Tell me about a time you had to work with someone whose style clashed with yours.
coach: They want to see your conflict resolution approach and emotional intelligence.

text: Describe a situation where your team disagreed on a key decision. How did you handle it?
coach: They're evaluating whether you can influence without authority and drive consensus.

text: Give me an example of a time you had to give tough feedback to a peer.
coach: They want evidence you can be direct while maintaining professional relationships.

text: Tell me about a cross-functional project where misalignment threatened the outcome.
coach: They're assessing your ability to navigate organizational complexity and competing priorities.

text: Describe a time you had to rebuild trust with a colleague after a breakdown.
coach: They want to see accountability, humility, and relationship repair skills.

text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager's decision. What did you do?
coach: They're testing whether you can disagree and commit without being passive-aggressive.

text: Give me an example of when you helped a struggling teammate without being asked.
coach: They want to see collaborative instinct and whether you lift others up proactively.

text: Describe a situation where you had to manage competing stakeholder expectations.
coach: They're looking for stakeholder management skill and your ability to say no diplomatically.

text: Tell me about your biggest professional failure and what you learned from it.
coach: They want genuine vulnerability plus evidence of a concrete behavior change afterward.

text: Describe a project that didn't go as planned. What would you do differently?
coach: They're testing your ability to reflect honestly without deflecting blame.

text: Tell me about a time you received critical feedback that was hard to hear.
coach: They want to see coachability and whether you internalize feedback or get defensive.

text: Give me an example of a goal you missed. How did you respond?
coach: They're assessing resilience and whether you take ownership of outcomes.

text: Describe a time you made a bad hire or misread a person. What happened?
coach: They want to see judgment growth and what you've refined in your assessment of people.

text: Tell me about a time you had to pivot your strategy mid-execution because your original plan wasn't working.
coach: They're testing adaptability and whether you cling to sunk costs or adjust quickly.

text: Describe a skill gap that held you back. How did you close it?
coach: They want evidence of self-directed growth and a learning mindset.

text: Tell me about a time you underestimated the complexity of something. What was the impact?
coach: They're probing your planning maturity and how you handle scope surprises.

text: Tell me about a time you led a project without formal authority.
coach: They want to see influence skills and whether you can mobilize people through vision alone.

text: Describe a situation where you identified a problem nobody else was addressing and took ownership.
coach: They're assessing proactive bias and whether you wait for permission or act.

text: Give me an example of a time you had to make a tough call with incomplete information.
coach: They want to see decisiveness under ambiguity and how you manage risk.

text: Tell me about a time you championed an unpopular idea that ultimately succeeded.
coach: They're testing conviction, persuasion skills, and whether you can stand alone when needed.

text: Describe how you onboarded or mentored someone who went on to do great work.
coach: They want to see multiplier behavior—do you develop others or just focus on yourself?

text: Tell me about a time you had to rally a demoralized team.
coach: They're evaluating emotional leadership and whether you can restore momentum.

text: Give me an example of when you pushed back on a request from leadership because it was the right thing to do.
coach: They want to see principled courage and whether you manage up effectively.

text: Describe a time you had to delegate something you were personally attached to.
coach: They're testing whether you can let go, trust others, and scale through delegation.

text: What's your superpower—the thing you do better than most people in your role?
coach: They want confident self-assessment backed by specific proof, not vague platitudes.

text: What's a real weakness you're actively managing?
coach: They're testing authenticity—they can smell fake weaknesses disguised as strengths.

text: What kind of work drains you, and how do you handle it?
coach: They want to understand your energy patterns and whether the role will burn you out.

text: What would your harshest critic say about working with you?
coach: They're probing self-awareness and whether you've internalized developmental feedback.

text: What's a skill you've had to work unusually hard to develop?
coach: They want to see grit and whether you can grow outside your natural talents.

text: How do you compensate for areas where you're not naturally strong?
coach: They're looking for strategic self-management—do you build systems or just wing it?

text: What type of feedback do you find hardest to act on?
coach: They want honesty about blind spots and evidence of growth orientation.

text: If I asked your teammates what makes you indispensable, what would they say?
coach: They're testing whether your perceived value aligns with what the role actually needs.

text: Why this company, and why now?
coach: They want to hear genuine research and alignment, not generic flattery.

text: What does your ideal work environment look like?
coach: They're checking culture fit and whether you'll thrive in their specific setup.

text: Where do you see yourself in three years?
coach: They want ambition that's realistic and aligned with the growth path they can offer.

text: What would make you turn down this offer?
coach: They're testing honesty and trying to surface deal-breakers early.

text: What's the most important thing for you in your next role?
coach: They want to understand your true motivators beyond compensation.

text: How do you stay motivated during repetitive or ambiguous stretches of work?
coach: They're probing intrinsic motivation and resilience during the unglamorous parts.

text: What's a company value of ours that resonates with you personally? Why?
coach: They want to see you've done homework and can connect values to lived experience.

text: What would you want to accomplish in your first 90 days here?
coach: They're assessing strategic thinking about ramp-up and early impact.

text: Walk me through a complex problem you broke down into manageable parts.
coach: They want to see structured thinking and how you decompose ambiguity.

text: Tell me about a time you had to make a decision with conflicting data.
coach: They're testing analytical rigor and comfort with uncertainty.

text: Describe a situation where you identified a root cause that others had missed.
coach: They want evidence of depth over surface-level thinking.

text: Tell me about a time you had to prioritize ruthlessly with limited resources.
coach: They're assessing trade-off thinking and strategic prioritization.

text: Give me an example of when you used data to change someone's mind.
coach: They want to see data fluency combined with persuasion skill.

text: Describe a time you had to solve a problem outside your area of expertise.
coach: They're testing resourcefulness and how quickly you ramp on unfamiliar territory.

text: Tell me about a time you anticipated a problem before it became critical.
coach: They want forward-thinking and proactive risk identification.

text: Describe a situation where the obvious solution was wrong. How did you figure that out?
coach: They're evaluating critical thinking and intellectual humility.

text: If you could have dinner with anyone alive or dead, who and why?
coach: They're testing quick thinking, personality, and whether you can be interesting under pressure.

text: Explain something complex that you know well to me as if I'm a smart 10-year-old.
coach: They want to see communication clarity and whether you can simplify without condescending.

text: What's a hill you'll die on professionally?
coach: They're probing your values and conviction—and whether those align with the team.

text: If you joined and in six months things weren't working out, what would likely be the reason?
coach: They want radical self-awareness about fit risks and potential friction points.

text: What's the most counterintuitive thing you've learned in your career?
coach: They're testing depth of reflection and whether you think originally.

text: If you had unlimited budget and one year, what problem would you solve?
coach: They want to see ambition, creativity, and what you genuinely care about.

text: What's a popular best practice in your field that you think is overrated?
coach: They're testing independent thinking and whether you follow dogma blindly.

text: Teach me something in the next 60 seconds.
coach: They want to see communication skill, enthusiasm, and how you perform on the spot.

text: Describe your ideal weekend morning.
coach: Practice vivid description and natural storytelling.

text: Talk about a book, show, or podcast that changed how you think.
coach: Practice explaining abstract ideas in a conversational, engaging way.

text: Describe a place you've visited that surprised you.
coach: Practice sensory storytelling and building a scene for your listener.

text: Tell me about a hobby you picked up as an adult.
coach: Practice showing enthusiasm and explaining your learning process.

text: Describe your relationship with technology outside of work.
coach: Practice balanced self-reflection without being overly rehearsed.

text: Talk about a meal or food experience that's stuck with you.
coach: Practice evoking emotion and sensory detail in a short monologue.

text: Describe a person who shaped who you are today.
coach: Practice telling a personal story with gratitude and specificity.

text: What's something you used to believe strongly but have since changed your mind about?
coach: Practice showing intellectual growth and narrating a belief transition.

text: Describe the best team or community you've ever been part of.
coach: Practice expressing what you value in groups without sounding generic.

text: Talk about a small daily ritual that keeps you grounded.
coach: Practice turning a simple topic into something genuinely interesting.

text: Describe a challenge you set for yourself that nobody asked you to do.
coach: Practice conveying internal motivation and self-driven narrative.

text: What would you do with an unexpected free month off?
coach: Practice speaking freely about hypotheticals with structure and energy.

text: Describe a moment that made you feel genuinely proud outside of work.
coach: Practice vulnerability and emotional range in a low-stakes context.

text: Talk about something you find fascinating that most people overlook.
coach: Practice making a niche topic accessible and contagiously interesting.

text: Describe your neighborhood or city to someone who's never been.
coach: Practice painting a picture with words and organizing spatial information.

text: Tell me about a tradition—family, cultural, or personal—that matters to you.
coach: Practice weaving meaning and personal identity into a brief narrative.
